description: About Supabase Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth. About the Role We're looking for a SDK Engineer - Python to join our SDK team and own how developers talk to Supabase from Python. You'll work closely with the rest of the SDK team, our Auth, Realtime, Storage, PostgREST, Functions, CLI and Docs teams, and the open-source community, helping us make the Python SDK a library Python developers genuinely enjoy using. Python developers reach Supabase from backend services, data pipelines, notebooks, and a growing number of AI agents and agent frameworks. The Python SDK is how all of them talk to the platform: database queries, auth, storage, realtime and edge functions, in both sync and async flavors. This is a library-authoring role, and the work happens in the open: public repos, public issue trackers, and API decisions whose consequences last for years. If you get satisfaction from a type checker that catches the bug before your users do, from an async client that cleans up after itself, and from an issue tracker that isn't a graveyard, you'll like it here. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions. What You'll Be Responsible For Build and evolve our Python SDK across database, auth, storage, realtime and functions, with both sync and async APIs that feel natural in Python. Start new things. Alongside the maintenance work, find what's missing, make the case for it, and build it. Nobody will hand you the list. Work in the open. Triage inbound issues, review and shepherd outside contributions, keep CI and release automation healthy, and hold a clear, kind line on scope. Own the typing experience. Make the SDK fully typed and checker-friendly, so autocomplete and static analysis stay correct in real codebases. Keep us honest across environments. Multiple Python versions, sync and async frameworks, workers, serverless and notebooks — with dependency ranges that don't fight our users' projects. Test it, don't assume it. Work on realtime. Long-lived websocket connections, reconnection, and subscription and presence semantics. Track the platform. When auth, realtime, storage, postgrest or edge functions ship a change, make sure the SDK reflects it, and that we say so in the changelog. Design in public. Write the RFCs, migration guides, release notes and docs. Treat a breaking change as a deprecation path plus a migration story, not a version bump. Make our SDK legible to AI coding agents , which are now a major consumer of it. You Might Be a Good Fit If You Know modern Python typing deeply. You use generics, protocols, overloads and TypedDict as design tools, run strict type checking, and fix type errors without reaching for Any . Have authored or maintained a published library with a public API and users outside your own company. You know what it costs to change something people depend on. Know the maintainer side of open source. Issue triage at volume, reviewing outside PRs, release automation, changelogs and semver, security reports, and saying no to a feature request without losing the person who asked. Are fluent in asyncio and have opinions on how a library should serve both sync and async callers. Know Python packaging for libraries: pyproject.toml , wheels, modern tooling, version support policy, and why libraries shouldn't pin their dependencies tightly. Test as a habit: unit, type-level and end-to-end against a real stack. Every fix comes with a regression test. Write well. Design docs, changelogs and issue replies are a large part of the output here, much of it public, and we're async by default. Have real autonomy: you find the important work, scope it, ship it, and say what you didn't do. Communicate clearly across both technical and non-technical audiences Have experience in async or globally distributed teams Are energized by solving real-world problems for developers Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and moving quickly Bonus points if you: have run a major-version migration for a public package, know your way around JWT/OAuth, have built integrations for AI agent frameworks, or have generated idiomatic clients from a schema. What We Offer Fully Remote We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world. ESOP Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together. Tech Allowance Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work. Health Benefits Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us. Annual Off-Sites Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year. Flexible Work We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when. Professional Development Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth. About the Team Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love. ~400 team members 60+ countries 20+ languages spoken Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F) 540,000+ community members We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

To stay at the forefront of consumer choice, Canonical - the company behind Ubuntu Linux - is expanding its investment into PC platform stability, reliability, and performance. The Canonical Kernel Team - those responsible for the build, maintenance, and distribution of the Linux kernel for Ubuntu - is looking for an individual to take ownership of aspects pertaining to the boot process, BIOS, UEFI, ACPI, and other platform firmware components as they pertain to the Ubuntu Linux kernel. By joining us you’ll be solving challenging problems within a talented team and a culture built for high performance. Our team out-think, out-work and out-care. We’re committed to delivering real change in the world - this isn’t easy, and in truth, we love that it’s hard. To find out more, visit our LinkedIn & Instagram . About the role Halter's component suppliers are predominantly based across Asia. The components they produce have to be right before they ever reach our contract manufacturers. When something is wrong, we need someone on the ground who can get to the root cause fast, push through to a real fix, and prevent it from happening again. The Supplier Quality Principal is Halter's senior technical authority embedded in Asia. You'll lead highly technical supplier audits, own complex quality problem-solving at our suppliers, and work directly with both suppliers and Halter's design teams to ensure that what comes off a supplier's production line meets the standard we set. You'll operate with a high degree of autonomy, covering a portfolio of suppliers across the region and acting as the technical bridge between our Asia supply base and the Halter team in Auckland. This is not a compliance role. Ticking audit checkboxes and filing reports is not what this job is about. The best person for this role is someone who goes deep: who can walk a production line and immediately identify what's controlling quality and what isn't, who can sit with a supplier's engineers and work through a failure mode from first principles, and who knows the difference between a corrective action that actually solves a problem and one that just looks good on paper. You'll report to the Head of Supplier Quality and work closely with Halter's hardware design and operations teams. When there's a quality issue in Asia that needs solving, you're the person we call. You'll be measured on the technical quality of audits, the speed and effectiveness of issue resolution at suppliers, and your ability to build supplier capability over time. What You'll Do Technical Supplier Auditing Lead technically rigorous audits of Halter's component suppliers across Asia, going well beyond system compliance to assess process control, measurement capability, and the reliability of how suppliers actually build and inspect parts. Identify the real drivers of quality performance at a supplier, not just the documented procedures, and develop clear, prioritised findings that distinguish between critical risks and cosmetic gaps. Conduct pre-qualification audits of new suppliers, assessing their technical capability and readiness to meet Halter's design and quality requirements before commitments are made. Run periodic surveillance audits to verify that corrective actions have been implemented effectively and that quality performance is being sustained. Develop and continuously improve Halter's audit methodology and supplier assessment criteria, ensuring audits capture what actually matters for component quality. Technical Problem Solving Own the resolution of complex quality issues at suppliers, using first-principles analysis to identify root cause and drive effective corrective actions rather than superficial fixes. When a production failure or OQC rejection occurs, lead rapid on-site analysis with supplier engineers and Halter's design team to understand the failure mode, assess risk to in-flight inventory, and define the fastest path to resolution. Work with suppliers to improve their process controls, measurement systems, and inspection methods so that quality issues are caught and corrected at source, not downstream. Coach supplier engineering teams to develop their own capability for root cause analysis and corrective action, building their ability to self-solve rather than depend on Halter for every issue. Escalate issues clearly and early when resolution is taking too long, a supplier is not engaging in good faith, or a quality risk to production is emerging. Quality Assurance Specifications Implement and maintain Halter's quality assurance specifications at suppliers, ensuring specifications are understood, accepted, and consistently applied across the production process. Work with Halter's hardware design team and the Head of Supplier Quality to refine QA specifications where field experience, audit findings, or supplier feedback reveals gaps or ambiguity. Ensure that when designs evolve, updated specifications are communicated to suppliers, implemented correctly, and re-validated before affected parts re-enter supply. Challenge specifications that are unclear, unmeasurable, or misaligned with what suppliers can realistically control, bringing engineering and operations teams to a better standard. Part Approval and Ongoing Compliance Support supplier-side part approval activities, ensuring new and revised components are formally validated against Halter's specifications before production release. Maintain a clear picture of approval status and open quality issues across the suppliers in your portfolio, tracking corrective actions to closure and flagging risks to supply continuity. Collaborate with the Head of Contract Manufacturing Quality when parts that pass supplier OQC fail IQC at our contract manufacturers, working to determine whether root cause sits with the supplier process, the OQC criteria, or the incoming inspection. Supplier Development Build genuine working relationships with quality and engineering counterparts at key suppliers, creating the trust and technical credibility that allows hard conversations to happen fast. Identify where suppliers have systemic capability gaps and develop structured improvement plans that address root cause, not symptoms. Share Halter's standards, expectations, and technical knowledge with suppliers in a way that builds their capability over time rather than creating dependency. What You Bring 15 or more years of experience in supplier quality or manufacturing quality for complex electromechanical hardware, with a proven track record of solving technically difficult quality problems at suppliers. Deep manufacturing and process engineering knowledge. You understand how parts are made, what drives process variation, and how to identify whether a supplier's process is actually in control. Exceptional audit capability. You conduct audits that go beneath the surface, uncover the real quality risks, and produce findings that drive meaningful improvement. Strong first-principles thinking. When you see a quality failure, you work back to the actual root cause, not the nearest plausible explanation. Experience with QA specification development and the ability to assess whether a specification is clear, measurable, and correctly implemented at a supplier. High proficiency in both English and Mandarin (written, verbal, and reading). You can work directly with Chinese engineers and leadership without translation. Comfortable operating autonomously across a portfolio of suppliers. You manage your own priorities, escalate the right things at the right time, and don't need close supervision to stay effective. Firm, fair, and direct with suppliers. You hold a high standard, push back on inadequate corrective actions, and maintain a relationship that is professional and productive even when conversations are hard. Willing to travel regularly across APAC. A significant portion of your time will be on-site at suppliers. A Master's degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline is preferred.
